messages.text: both sides of ∥ write credits; rules in parallel must write disjoint state

explain: First bug: take and give both write credits, so they cannot be ∥. With take ≫ give: 1. take subtracts one credit. 2. give sees the new value and adds one back. A send and a response in the same cycle leave credits unchanged: in the simulation, io_credits is 3 at cycle 10 and still 3 at cycle 11. It compiles now, but simulate it further: io_ok still drops, at cycle 6 (see the second answer).

Second bug: with 4 requests out, credits is 0 at cycle 5 and send is high. In order: 1. take runs: inflight < 5 holds (4 < 5), so it fires and credits wraps to 7 (3 bits). At cycle 6 io_credits is 7, io_inflight is 5, and io_ok is low. With inflight < 4, equivalent to credits != 0, take does not fire at cycle 5 and io_ok stays high in every cycle.
diff: -  Bool canSend = send && inflight < 5;   -- at most 4 in flight
+  Bool canSend = send && inflight < 4;   -- at most 4 in flight
